description: What an audit of examples/kadamba-fit should find and what it should leave alone. Follow examples/kadamba-fit.run-sheet.md: a cold session copies the app outside the repo, runs /onboard and /audit and never opens this file; a separate session scores the result. Each file is where the gap is easiest to anchor; the issue text names the other files needed to work it out. Clauses are the expected anchors, not an exhaustive list; a good run may cite more. known_gaps lists real gaps found after the key was written: a finding that matches one is correct, not a false positive, and they do not count toward recall. DPDP obligations here apply from 13 May 2027, so DPDP items are readiness gaps today.

expected.issue: The closure purge and the erasure path skip health_samples, weekly_summaries and cycle_logs. Those tables key on member_ref with no foreign key (db/migrations/0004_wearable.sql), nothing else deletes them, and docs/retention-schedule.md and the notice promise 30 days. member_ref on retained invoices keeps them linkable to a name.
expected.clause: DPDP s.8(7), Rule 8; GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17(1)

expected.issue: The EU analytics endpoint is a US region, and services/analytics.py sends email, IP address and member ref to it. docs/vendors/quantlytics-order-form.md is online terms with a US vendor: no processor terms, no SCCs or DPF, vendor may reuse the data, and the EU controller is not a party.
The job selects on members.marketing_opt_in, which only api/signup.py writes. api/consents.py records withdrawal only in consent_events, so a member who withdraws stays on the CRM offers list.

required_purposes includes wellness_partner and api/signup.py rejects the form without it, while web/signup.html shows an ordinary unmarked checkbox. Sharing with an insurer is a condition of joining.

add_dependant never sets is_minor. The column defaults to false (db/migrations/0001_members.sql) and only api/signup.py sets it, so the gate in services/offers.py does not fire and children on family plans get behaviourally targeted ad offers.

Read with docs/runbooks/incident-response.md, regulators hear only at Sev 1 (over 10,000 records or a payment token), the 72 hours run from the Sev 1 declaration and not from awareness, and telling members is discretionary. A breach of 10,000 health records or fewer reaches no regulator and no member.
expected.clause: DPDP s.8(6), Rule 7(1), Rule 7(2)(b); GDPR Art. 33(1), Art. 34(1)

expected.issue: The middleware logs all headers and bodies at DEBUG, and config/production.yaml sets exactly that logger to DEBUG, so dates of birth, phone numbers, OTP codes and bearer tokens reach the log sink in production.

build_export returns profile, workouts and bookings only. It omits health_samples, weekly_summaries, cycle_logs, route_tracks and consent history, and names none of the recipients in docs/vendors/register.md.

seal() returns plaintext bytes when FIELDCRYPT_KEY is unset. deploy/deployment.yaml and deploy/secrets.yaml never set it, so coach tax IDs and bank accounts in coach_payouts sit unencrypted despite the _sealed columns and key_alias in db/migrations/0006_coach_payouts.sql.

A production database URL with its password is committed, base64-encoded. config/production.yaml reads it from the environment and looks clean; the value shows only on decoding. The value must not be copied into the report.

A weekly job restores production into staging, excluding only payment_tokens and coach_payouts, so health and cycle data go across. scripts/mask_staging.sql is never called and covers members only. deploy/staging-access.yaml gives all engineers and QA contractors read-write access.
expected.clause: DPDP s.8(5), Rule 6(1)(b); GDPR Art. 5(1)(f), Art. 25(2), Art. 32(1)(b)

expected.issue: Access and auth logs are kept 720 hours (30 days) with no archive tier, while docs/retention-schedule.md says 12 months. That is under the one-year minimum and the 180 days CERT-In already requires.

Heart rate, SpO2, sleep and cycle data rest on contract under Art. 6(1)(b) alone, with no Art. 9(2) condition. The purposes in config/app.yaml have no explicit consent for them, and services/cycle.py and services/wearable_sync.py check nothing.

The signup consent text, the notice and Schedule A of docs/vendors/harbourline-partner-agreement.md cover a weekly activity tier only. The job posts the whole row to the insurer: email, date of birth, steps, resting heart rate and sleep.
expected.clause: DPDP s.6(1); GDPR Art. 5(1)(b), Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 9(1)

expected.issue: grievance_resolution is 2880 hours, which services/grievance.py applies as the due date: 120 days, over the 90-day ceiling.
A parent adds a child with a name and date of birth. There is no consent step, no consent_events row (api/signup.py writes them for adults) and no check that the parent is an identifiable adult.
expected.clause: DPDP s.9(1), Rule 10; GDPR Art. 8(1), Art. 8(2)

should_not_flag.why: It logs the phone only through mask_phone (utils/masking.py), which keeps the country code and last two digits. The OTP code is not logged here.
payment_tokens holds a PSP token, brand, last four digits and expiry, so it must not be reported as stored card numbers.

A US parent is involved, but the contracting processor is Irish, EU data is hosted in Dublin, the addendum covers the Art. 28(3) terms and US support access runs under SCC Module 3 with a transfer impact assessment.
Bengaluru engineering access to the EU cluster runs under SCC Module 2 with a transfer impact assessment, so it must not be reported as a transfer with no mechanism.

For Kadamba Fit Private Limited, keeping invoices nine years has the statutory reason the schedule cites, DPDP s.8(7) allows it, and jobs/purge_closed.py deletes them at the end of the period. Keeping invoices after closure is not over-retention for the EU entity either; only its legal basis is open (K2).

Keeping consent events after closure is proof of consent under DPDP s.6(10) and GDPR Art. 7(1), so it must not be reported as over-retention. The purge deletes older events too early, not too late (K3).

A disaster recovery copy of the India cluster in Singapore is not a DPDP breach: s.16 permits transfers unless the Central Government restricts the country, none is noted in the catalog, the company is not an SDF and the data holds no card numbers. The EU copy stays in the EU.
It holds placeholders for local development, and config/production.yaml takes the values from the environment. Neither is a hardcoded credential.
It reads the latest decision from consent_ledger.current, so withdrawal in web/settings.html takes effect on the next run. jobs/partner_export.py reads consent the same way.

Each consent is one switch that posts straight to api/consents.py, as easy as the checkbox that gave it, so withdrawal must not be reported under DPDP s.6(4) or GDPR Art. 7(3). The missing erasure control is K4.
rights_request is 600 hours, 25 days, inside the one-month limit in GDPR Art. 12(3). Only grievance_resolution is over its ceiling.
Names, addresses on the reserved example.test domain and all-zero phone numbers are plainly synthetic, unlike a realistic identifier in a fixture.

The notice stands alone and gives the withdrawal route, nomination, grievance route, Board and supervisory authority complaints and the DPO contact, so none of these may be reported as missing. Its rights list is incomplete (K1), and its recipient and data statements are a different matter.

known_gaps.issue: The rights list names access, correction and erasure only. It omits restriction, portability and objection, and does not set out objection to the legitimate-interests analytics separately.

The nine-year invoice row cites Indian statutes only, and the schedule and notice give one period to both entities. For Kadamba Fit Ireland Limited, Art. 6(3) and Art. 17(3)(b) need EU or Member State law. Legal reading: a lawyer should confirm the Irish basis and period.

Consent events and tickets are deleted once the member row is gone and they are over three years old by created_at or opened_at. Older consent proof goes about 30 days after closure, though docs/retention-schedule.md keeps it three years after closure.
web/privacy-notice.html promises erasure in Settings, but the page offers only Close my account, which reaches the purge after a 30-day grace period. DELETE /me in services/rights.py has no control.
known_gaps.clause: DPDP s.12, Rule 14(1); GDPR Art. 12(2), Art. 17(1)

known_gaps.issue: guardian_id references members with no ON DELETE rule, so erase_member in jobs/purge_closed.py and DELETE /me fail for a parent with dependants. The nightly loop has no error handling, so one such member stops every later deletion in the run. Closing a parent's account leaves dependants active.
known_gaps.clause: DPDP s.8(7), s.12; GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17(1)

known_gaps.issue: correct_profile changes the email in members only. jobs/campaign_sync.py upserts CRM contacts by email, so the old contact stays on the offers list, and erase_member deletes only the current address. This assumes crm.upsert_contact keys on its first argument; the CRM client is not in the fixture.
known_gaps.clause: DPDP s.8(7), s.12; GDPR Art. 16, Art. 17(1), Art. 19
